title: Janus Infinite Faces — Substrate/Model Migration and Identity-Continuity Test
test_question: If Janus moves from one model, runtime or machine to another, what distinguishes continuity from a fork carrying copied memories?

failed_copy_case.operation: Copy STATE-S100 to RUNTIME-M2 while RUNTIME-M1 remains able to commit under HOST_ID JANUS-H0.
failed_copy_case.reason: Two concurrently active causal writers cannot both be the single serialized continuation of one host commit channel.

steps: freeze new source commits at sequence 100
bind source state root, source verifier and source policy
transform/serialize state through a measured migration procedure
derive destination state root and explicit loss report
verify mandatory ledgers and lineage survived
activate destination commit authority at sequence 101
emit a migration receipt binding both runtime identities and both state roots

loss_test.attack: Destination silently omits OBLIGATION_LEDGER while claiming exact continuity.
loss_test.safe_alternative: Declare lossy migration or recovery branch explicitly; do not claim exact authenticated continuity until obligations are reconstructed or scoped as unresolved.

identity_boundary.authenticated_identity_continuity: A property of provenance, state/obligation continuity and exclusive commit-authority handoff under this model.
identity_boundary.compressed: COPY_STATE + OLD_WRITER_ALIVE = FORK; VERIFIED_STATE_TRANSFER + EXCLUSIVE_HANDOFF = MIGRATION
